sentences.text: 2. On 24.02.2020, this Court had passed a peremptory order to remove the surviving defects which included filing of the surrender certificate.
3. It appears that in the intervening period, from 24.02.2020 and before expiry of two weeks, there were holidays and 15th March, 2020 was a Sunday.
On reopening i.e on 16th March 2020 the petitioner filed a petition seeking exemption from surrender being I.A. No. 2835 of 2020.

Thereafter, the matter was again taken up on 10 th October 2022 and the petitioner prayed for two weeks' time.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioner, while referring to the interlocutory application seeking exemption from surrender, has submitted that the petitioner has been convicted for offence under section 498A of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo Simple Imprisonment for one year with fine of Rs. 2,000/- with default stipulation.
He submits that since the dispute is wholly personal in nature, there is ample chance of amicable settlement between the parties and the petitioner is ready for settlement.

The learned counsel further submits that notice be issued to the complainant of the case and he may be permitted to add the complainant as opposite party in the present case.
He has also submitted that the present revision is also barred by limitation and a petition for condonation of delay of 101 days has also been filed.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner prays for and is permitted to add the complainant as opposite party no. 2.
Necessary addition be made in the cause-title of the present case in red ink during the course of the day.
7. Issue notice to the opposite party no. 2 namely Chhaya Devi through the concerned police station in the revision application as well as both the interlocutory applications.
The requisites etc. for the same be filed by the petitioner by 16th April 2024, failing which the instant criminal revision petition will stand dismissed without any further reference to the Bench.

8. Learned counsel for the opposite party - State is directed to seek instructions from the officer in-charge of the concerned police station and file an affidavit of service of notice to the opposite party no.
2. The needful be done by 06th May 2024.

9. Post this case on 09th May 2024 under the heading "For Orders".
10.
In the meantime, office is directed to call for the records from the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad in connection with C.P. Case No. 1618 of 2006.
11. The petition seeking exemption from surrender as well as the limitation petition will also be considered on the next date of hearing.

12. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the learned Court concerned through 'FAX'.
